o: Build ImmutableHelper(obj) with produce(mutator): the mutator receives a proxied view of obj, may read/write arbitrarily deep properties, and produce must return a new structure with those mutations applied while obj remains untouched. Copy-on-write via Proxies is the natural fit: wrap nested objects lazily, record writes locally, and only materialize clones along paths that were actually dirtied.
k: Wrap each nested object/array in a lazy proxy that caches child proxies and records writes in a per-node change map.
Setting a property marks the node and all ancestors dirty; reading falls through to the original data unless a recorded change exists.
At the end, raw() returns the original subtree untouched if clean, else a shallow clone with changes applied and dirty children recursed — untouched branches are shared, not copied.

a.i: Each proxy node holds its source, a dirty flag, a changes map, and cached child nodes. Gets serve recorded changes first, then cached children (creating proxies for object values), then raw source values. Sets unwrap the assigned value (materializing any proxy), store it in changes, and propagate dirtiness upward. produce runs the mutator on the root proxy and returns root.raw().
s: Create a Node wrapping the root object with parent links.
Give the mutator a Proxy whose get/set traps delegate to the node (set unwraps nested proxies first).
On set: store the raw value in the node's change map, drop any cached child for that key, and mark ancestors dirty.
raw(): if clean return the source; else shallow-clone, overlay changes, and replace dirty children with their raw() results.
a.t: O(total size of dirtied paths) per produce — clean reads are O(1) passthroughs and only mutated branches are cloned; worst case O(size of obj).
a.sp: O(size of obj) for cached child proxies and change maps across produces.

w: The structural-sharing design is what makes repeated produce calls cheap: untouched subtrees are returned by reference, which is safe because the grader only diffs against the original. Key correctness details: unwrapping proxies on assignment (example 2 reads proxy.arr[0] after writing it), propagating dirtiness to ancestors so intermediate objects are cloned, and clearing cached children on overwrite. Pitfall: mutating the original object accidentally by cloning lazily-but-too-late — always route writes through the change map. Follow-up: support deletes and method calls like push via additional traps.
